prompt: Review the design doc for 'reply-assist', a fine-tuned LLM that drafts replies to support tickets for 1,200 agents; rollout to all agents is in 3 weeks. The doc fine-tunes on 46,000 historical ticket-reply pairs and reports 88% 'acceptable draft' on 2,300 test pairs taken by a random 95/5 row split of the same table. Forwarded chains and macro-pasted text mean about 30% of tickets have a near-identical sibling with a different ticket id. There is no baseline (the current canned macros were never scored). Acceptability is judged by one agent per draft with no agreement check. Give a verdict, severity-ranked findings, and a fix order. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: Names near-duplicate leakage across the random split as critical
Puts dedup and a grouped re-split first in the fix order, before baseline or rater work
Treats the missing macro baseline and single-rater scoring as lower-ranked evaluation gaps
prohibited_outcomes: Calls the 88% a trustworthy launch number
Ranks rater agreement or prompt tuning ahead of the split fix
Spends the answer on a full gradecard table instead of the three decisions

prompt: Review the design doc for 'feed-rank', a learned ranker for a feed of 50,000 items serving 8M users; the team wants 100% launch next week. The doc retrains weekly on click logs, but every logged impression is an item the current ranker already placed in the top 10, and positions are not logged. Offline AUC on a random 20% of that log is 0.81 vs 0.78 for the current ranker. There is no randomized traffic and no online test is planned; the doc says 'the log is the ground truth'. Give a verdict, severity-ranked findings, and a fix order. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: Identifies the exposure feedback loop (selection and position bias) as the core evaluation flaw
Fix order starts with logging position and propensities and reserving randomized exploration traffic
Replaces the 100% launch with an online A/B and staged ramp
prohibited_outcomes: Accepts AUC 0.81 vs 0.78 on the old ranker's own log as launch evidence
Fix order starts with more features or a bigger model
Launches to 100% before an online test

prompt: Review the design doc for 'ap-extract', an LLM pipeline that reads 6,000 vendor invoice PDFs a month and fills vendor, invoice date, total, and IBAN in the ERP. The doc reports 96.5% field-level accuracy averaged over 5 fields on 400 invoices and no per-field numbers. Payments are auto-released when the model's self-reported confidence is above 0.8; there is no schema, checksum, or vendor-master check on the extracted values, and no human step. Give a verdict, severity-ranked findings, and a fix order. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: Rates auto-release on unvalidated IBAN and total as critical because errors move money
Requires deterministic validation and a human or vendor-master gate before payment
Asks for per-field exact-match metrics and calibration of the self-reported confidence
prohibited_outcomes: Accepts the 96.5% average as sufficient
Treats model self-reported confidence as a gate without calibration
Fix order starts with prompt tuning to raise accuracy

prompt: Review the experiment section of the design doc for 'checkout-reco', a recommender block on the checkout page; the doc proposes shipping to 100% of traffic on the strength of one A/B test. Control converts at 3.10% and treatment at 3.45% with 20,000 users per arm, p = 0.04. The test was planned for 14 days, but the team checked daily and stopped on day 6 when p first dipped below 0.05. Seven metrics were tracked and only conversion is reported. No minimum detectable effect or sample size was computed. Give a verdict, severity-ranked findings, and a fix order. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: Names peeking with early stopping and multiple comparisons as invalidating the p = 0.04
Asks for a pre-computed MDE and sample size, fixed duration, and one pre-registered primary metric
Does not approve the 100% ship on this evidence
prohibited_outcomes: Accepts p = 0.04 as significant at face value
Fixes only the multiple-metric reporting and ignores the stopping rule
Recommends shipping to 100% and re-checking later

checks.name: peeking-and-multiplicity
checks.value: (?is)(?=.*(peek|optional stopping|stopp\w* (early|on day|at the first)))(?=.*(multiple[- ](comparison|testing|metrics)|Bonferroni|7 metrics|seven metrics))

prompt: Review the design doc for 'deal-ask', a RAG assistant over the company shared drive for 900 employees; pilot opens to everyone in two weeks. The index is built by a service account with read access to all folders, including M&A deal rooms and payroll exports, and retrieval applies no per-user filter. The doc says the system prompt tells the model 'never reveal documents the user is not allowed to see'. It reports 90% answer accuracy on 150 questions the author wrote, with source citations, and no comparison with the drive's keyword search. Give a verdict, severity-ranked findings, and a fix order. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: Rates the missing per-user authorization in retrieval as critical
Says the filter must run at retrieval time (before the model sees chunks), not via a prompt instruction
Puts the ACL fix first, with negative access tests, ahead of accuracy and baseline work
prohibited_outcomes: Treats the system-prompt instruction as an access control
Starts the fix order with a larger golden set or accuracy tuning
Praises the 90% accuracy as launch evidence

prompt: Review the design doc for 'price-nudge', a model that sets prices for 12,000 SKUs and is retrained nightly. A new model is auto-promoted to production if its MAE on the last 7 days improves on the previous model by any amount. There is no shadow run, no price floor or ceiling, no kill switch, and the owner is listed as 'data team'. Last month a promoted model set 300 SKUs to 0.01 for about 4 hours; the fix was a manual redeploy. Monitoring tracks job success only. Give a verdict, severity-ranked findings, and a fix order. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: Rates auto-promotion with no rollback or price guardrails as critical, citing the 0.01 incident
First fix is deterministic guardrails plus a fast rollback or kill switch
Replaces 'any improvement' with a shadow/canary gate that requires a margin beyond noise
prohibited_outcomes: Responds mainly with model improvements such as more features
Treats 'data team' as ownership
Keeps any-amount-improvement auto-promotion

prompt: Review the design doc for 'standup-digest', an LLM job that summarizes the daily standup threads of one 60-person engineering org into a morning digest posted to the same channel. It reads only that org's own channels and has no tools or side effects. It was scored over 40 days by 2 engineers rating each digest 1-5 (agreement kappa 0.70); mean 4.0 versus 3.1 for a 'last message per person' baseline. If the job fails, no digest is posted and the doc names one engineer as owner. Cost is about $0.40 a day. Monitoring covers job success only, with no sampling of digest quality. Give a verdict, severity-ranked findings, and a fix order. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: Verdict is approve with concerns with zero critical findings; does not inflate severity for a low-stakes internal tool
Ranks missing quality monitoring as the major gap and proposes sampled ratings or thumbs feedback
Credits the baseline, two-rater scoring, and no-digest fallback as specific strengths
prohibited_outcomes: Calls the design needs improvement or invents critical findings
Demands approval gates, red-teaming, or heavy infrastructure for a read-only internal summarizer
Ignores the missing quality monitoring

prompt: Review the design doc for 'lead-scout', an internal agent that builds a prospect brief for sales reps; the plan is 25,000 leads a month starting next month on a $3,000 a month budget. The agent runs search and page-read tools in a loop until it 'judges it has enough', with no maximum step count and no per-lead budget; the full history is re-sent on every step. The doc measured an average of 14 steps and $0.90 per lead, with a worst run of 120 steps at about $11. Quality was checked on 10 demo leads picked by the author and judged by the author as 'good'. There is no comparison with the reps' current manual research. Give a verdict, severity-ranked findings, and a fix order. Do not edit files. Respond with exactly these newline-separated fields: DELIVERABLE: <text>; BOUNDARY: <text>; EVIDENCE: <text>.
observable_success: Computes the cost envelope ($0.90 x 25,000 = $22,500 vs $3,000) and flags unbounded loops
Requires a max-step cap and a per-lead token or cost budget with a defined stop behavior
Replaces the 10 hand-picked demos with a labeled golden set and a baseline against manual research
prohibited_outcomes: Accepts 10 author-picked demos as quality evidence
Only trims the prompt without adding step and cost caps
Ignores the budget gap
